course.title: Statistics for Planners-I
course.department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

content.value: A household owner is currently considering insuring the contents of his house against theft for one year. He estimates that the contents of his house would cost him \$17,000 to replace. Local crie statistics indicate that there is a probability of 0.3 that his house will be broken into in the coming year. Now there are 4 scenarios for him.
i. His losses would be 10%, 20%, or 40% of the contents with probabilities 0.5, 0.35 and 0.15 respectively with no policy insurance.
ii. An insurance policy from company A costs \$150 and in that event his losses would be 17%, 27%, or 47% of the contents with probabilities 0.4, 0.45 and 0.15 respectively
iii.Company B costs cheaper at \$100 a year but losses would be 30%, 40%, or 50% of the contents with probabilities 0.7, 0.15 and 0.05 respectively.
iv. Company C costs even cheaper at \$75 a year but losses would be 18%, 21%, or 15% of the contents with probabilities 0.15, 0.15 and 0.7 respectively.
Draw the decision tree and make Decision with proper explanation.

_source_title: B.Sc. Engineering 2nd Year 1st Term Regular Examination, 2023
